source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's Florence, Kentucky campus, CIN6, is the largest data center on Kentucky's public record at 5 MW of IT capacity, but that ranking reflects disclosure more than scale.

The facility publishes 5 MW of IT load and 143,000 square feet of technical space. It does not publish a rack count, an accelerator count, or a power density. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 5 MW supports roughly 125 racks. At 10 kW per rack it supports about 500. The published figure alone does not say which the building was designed for, so any rack estimate is a conversion the reader makes, not one the operator endorses.

The certifications, PCI DSS, HIPAA, ISO 27001, FISMA, SSAE 16 Type II, and Green Globes, qualify the campus for categories of workload. They do not name a tenant. No tenant list is published, so the certifications establish what the building is permitted to host, not who is inside it.

Kentucky has five mapped facilities, three of which publish a megawatt figure, totaling 9.55 MW across the state. CIN6 ranks first by published capacity. That is a statement about disclosure as much as construction, because most mapped facilities in the state publish no figure at all. A 5 MW campus is small against the hundreds of megawatts at the largest AI sites, and its relevance to AI scaling in Kentucky rests on it being the only large published number the state currently offers.
